statement: Let W ∈ R[c1, . . . , ck] be nonnegative on Rk, where k ≥ 1, and let C be a nonempty subset of Z = {W = 0} that is both open and closed in Z. Choose an odd integer ℓ ≥ 3 with ℓ > deg W, and put G(c) = k X i=1 cℓ+1 i , Hw(c) = G(c) + (ℓ + 1)wW(c). In the quotient by cℓ i + w ∂W ∂ci = 0 (1 ≤ i ≤ k), (6.10) form the coordinate multiplication polynomials Pi(w, T) = det(TI − Mci ) = X j Pi,j(T)wj . (6.11) For each i, let ji be the largest index for which Pi,ji ̸= 0. There exists c∗ ∈ C such that Pi,ji (c∗ i ) = 0 (1 ≤ i ≤ k). If W is a controlled family of integer polynomials, k is polynomially bounded, and ℓ is short and computable in polynomial time, then the polynomials Pi and Pi,j are uniformly controlled.
